newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cements, banks push Egypt shares to new record.
newsitem.headline: Cements, banks push Egypt shares to new record.

text.p: Gains in the blue-chip cement and banking sectors took the Cairo stock exchange on Tuesday to a 13th straight record high.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 1.72 percent up at 394.6 points, which is 30.7 percent more than its level at the start of the year.

Turnover was a heavy 205.12 million pounds ($60.33 million), dominated by nine transactions worth more than 90 million pounds in rarely-traded firm Lecico Ceramic and Sanitary Ware. The firm's shares closed unchanged at 6090 pounds
A handful of deals worth $13.49 million in the dollar denominated shares of Alexandria National Iron and Steel helped boost the day's volume but the stock also ended unchanged at $49.4.
Trading was also active in the popular cement firms and most ended the day firmer, except for Helwan Portland Cement which shed 0.6 to 79.4 in busy trade.

Suez Cement was the most active stock in its sector and rose 1.6 pounds to 76.6 in trading worth 9.2 million pounds. Egyptian Portland Tora Cement also gained 0.51 to 91.5 and Amriyah Cement ended unchanged at 86 after rising to 90.3 during the session.
But the banking sector was the day's best performer with share prices ending higher across the board.

National Societe Generale Bank was the biggest gainer, rising 41.13 to 868 while Egyptian American Bank was the most active and shares ended 4.11 pounds higher at 154.11 after trading worth 4.23 million pounds.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) rose 30 pounds to 630 and Misr International Bank/MIBANK gained 8.2 to 592 pounds. Watany Bank also rose 3.31 to 69.55.
Partially-privatised Nile Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries was also among the day's most traded stocks with deals worth 9.35 million but share prices closed 0.5 pounds lower at 62.5 pounds.
The state sold a minority stake in the firm about two years ago and has since said that it would not give up majority control of the drugs sector due to its "strategic nature".
The index for openly traded firms rose to 651.87 points from 639.56 on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 261.75 from 257.66 points.
Out of the 74 shares traded, 49 gained, 5 lost and 20 ended the day unchanged.
